edges.description: Hippocampal sclerosis is the primary histopathological lesion in drug-resistant temporal lobe epilepsy and is associated with recurrent mesial temporal lobe seizures.

Epitranscriptomic m6A dysregulation in TLE hippocampal tissue—marked by upregulated writer/eraser machinery and predominant transcript hypermethylation that inversely correlates with protein pathway activation—modulates cellular and temporal network excitability, and pharmacologically elevating m6A via FTO inhibition decreases PTZ-induced seizure susceptibility in mice.

Epitranscriptomic m6A RNA methylation changes in TLE modulate seizure thresholds, with pharmacological elevation of m6A via FTO inhibition (recreating the post-status epilepticus hypermethylation state) decreasing pentylenetetrazol-induced seizure susceptibility and severity in mice.
Altered excitation/inhibition balance in temporal and frontal cortical networks is associated with temporal lobe epilepsy and recurrent focal seizures.
Altered excitation/inhibition balance in the left entorhinal and bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortices correlates with lower performance on short-term verbal memory.
Microstructural damage to thalamocortical pathways is associated with poorer executive function performance in temporal lobe epilepsy.

nodes.description: Dysregulation of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) RNA methylation in temporal lobe epilepsy involves upregulation of m6A writers and erasers with predominant transcript hypermethylation in hippocampal tissue, where m6A levels inversely correlate with protein pathway activation across metabolic and autophagic pathways; recreating this post-status epilepticus hypermethylation state via pharmacological FTO inhibition (FB23-2) in naive mice challenged with pentylenetetrazol (PTZ) decreases acute seizure susceptibility and severity.

evidence.reference_title: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) dysregulation contributes to network excitability in temporal lobe epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: Specifically, our results suggest that m6A levels inversely correlate with protein pathway activation.

evidence.reference_title: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) dysregulation contributes to network excitability in temporal lobe epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: Finally, we show that elevated levels of m6A decrease seizure susceptibility and severity in mice.

nodes.description: Temporal lobe epilepsy is associated with altered excitation/inhibition balance across temporal and connected cortical regions, with molecular correlates implicating both GABAergic and glutamatergic signaling.

evidence.reference_title: Excitation/Inhibition balance relates to cognitive function and gene expression in temporal lobe epilepsy: a high density EEG assessment with aperiodic exponent.
evidence.snippet: Patients with temporal lobe epilepsy showed a significantly larger exponent, corresponding to inhibition-directed E/I balance, in bilateral frontal and temporal regions.

evidence.reference_title: Excitation/Inhibition balance relates to cognitive function and gene expression in temporal lobe epilepsy: a high density EEG assessment with aperiodic exponent.
evidence.snippet: Limited to patients with temporal lobe epilepsy, we detected a significant correlation between the exponent and the cortical expression of GABRA1, GRIN2A, GABRD, GABRG2, KCNA2 and PDYN genes.

nodes.description: Impairment of executive functions (including mental flexibility, inhibition, and shifting) associated with microstructural disruption of thalamocortical pathways.

evidence.reference_title: Thalamocortical Connections and Executive Function in Pediatric Temporal and Frontal Lobe Epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: In patients with temporal lobe epilepsy, poorer performance on all measures of executive function was associated with DTI indices reflective of damaged/less developed pathways.

nodes.description: In mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, hippocampal sclerosis is characterized by selective loss of pyramidal neurons and reactive gliosis predominantly in the CA1 and CA4/CA3 subfields with relative sparing of CA2 and the subiculum, remodeling mesial temporal circuitry and promoting seizure generation.

evidence.reference_title: Proteomic profile differentiating between mesial temporal lobe epilepsy with and without hippocampal sclerosis.
evidence.snippet: We confirmed histologically that all MTLE-HS cases examined exhibited severe neuronal cell loss and remarkable astrocytic gliosis in the hippocampi.

evidence.reference_title: International consensus classification of hippocampal sclerosis in temporal lobe epilepsy: A Task Force report from the <scp>ILAE</scp> Commission on Diagnostic Methods
evidence.snippet: Hippocampal sclerosis (HS) is the most frequent histopathology encountered in patients with drug‐resistant temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE).

evidence.reference_title: N6-methyladenosine (m6A) dysregulation contributes to network excitability in temporal lobe epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: Hippocampal sclerosis was defined as neuronal loss and gliosis primarily involving the CA1 and CA4/3 subfields with relative resistance of the CA2 region and sparing of the subiculum (if the latter were included in the resected specimen).

nodes.description: Verbal short-term memory can be impaired and correlates with altered excitation/inhibition balance in entorhinal and frontal cortical regions.

evidence.reference_title: Excitation/Inhibition balance relates to cognitive function and gene expression in temporal lobe epilepsy: a high density EEG assessment with aperiodic exponent.
evidence.snippet: Lower E/I in the left entorhinal and bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortices corresponded to a lower performance of short-term verbal memory.

nodes.description: Recurrent focal seizures originating from temporal lobe networks, often with impaired awareness and temporal-lobe semiology.

evidence.snippet: Initial management of patients with temporal lobe epilepsy is with antiepileptic drugs, but these control seizures in only half the patients.

evidence.reference_title: A randomized, controlled trial of surgery for temporal-lobe epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: At one year, the cumulative proportion of patients who were free of seizures impairing awareness was 58 percent in the surgical group and 8 percent in the medical group (P<0.001).

nodes.description: Vulnerable thalamocortical pathways can contribute to cognitive dysfunction in temporal lobe epilepsy, indicating that the disorder affects distributed neural circuits beyond the temporal focus itself.

evidence.reference_title: Thalamocortical Connections and Executive Function in Pediatric Temporal and Frontal Lobe Epilepsy.
evidence.snippet: Our results give insight into vulnerable neural networks in pediatric focal epilepsy and suggest thalamocortical pathway damage as a potential mechanism of executive function impairment in temporal lobe epilepsy but not frontal lobe epilepsy.
